content.title: About
content.content: Green seedless grapes are fresh berries of the grapevine (Vitis vinifera) cultivated without seeds. They have a sweet‑tart flavor, crisp texture, and bright green color. Grapes are eaten raw, added to salads, desserts, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green seedless grapes are often bred specifically for fresh consumption.
Seedless varieties are created through genetic techniques that suppress seed development.
Grapes are one of the oldest cultivated plants – they have been grown for over 8,000 years.
Sugar content in green grapes is usually lower than in red varieties, making them slightly less caloric.
Vineyards can produce vines that live for more than 50 years, sometimes even centuries.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Grapes contain resveratrol, quercetin, and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids and potassium contribute to lower blood pressure and improved vessel function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Grapes provide vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: With more than 80 % water content, grapes help maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to grapes.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of grapes can raise blood glucose levels, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If not organic, pesticide residues may remain on the skin; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat grapes fresh, add them to fruit salads, yogurt, smoothies, and desserts. They can be frozen for homemade sorbet or used as a garnish for dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grapes in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or an open container to keep them dry. Properly stored, they stay fresh for 7–10 days. Remove any spoiled berries to prevent the rest from rotting.
